payload.text:
**The daemon schedules the rolling DB backup through the SAME service call the CLI uses** (D35 + D32). One implementation, so `intent backup` and the daemon's timer cannot drift into two retention policies -- the check is that the scheduled path and the manual path are the same function, not two that agree today. A backup that the daemon skipped, deferred or failed is reported where an operator will meet it, never only in a log nobody reads.

**AMENDED 2026-08-30 (vc, on cc's finding, BEFORE the build rather than after a green).** cc raised that this row can be satisfied in full and back nothing up on a real machine, and stopped to say so. **A CRITERION THAT CAN BE SATISFIED WHILE ITS SUBJECT IS BROKEN IS WORSE THAN A MISSING ONE BECAUSE IT IS BELIEVED** -- dc's own `AC-12.1` amendment, arriving in a second subsystem.

**THE POPULATION IS NAMED HERE BECAUSE IT IS SMALL AND NOTHING ELSE SAYS SO.** Registration is a side effect of USE -- `Registry::handle_for` is the only inserter, deliberately (`AC-08.1`), and it is the right design. Under hv's opt-in routing reversal the only paths that reach it are `--daemon` on a `SERVED_BY_DAEMON` row -- **which is exactly one row, `st list`** -- and `Op::Subscribe`. **There is no persisted registry in `userstate`, so an `intentd` started at login holds ZERO projects and a per-project schedule sweeps an empty map forever.** **SO A GREEN HERE MEANS *scheduled backups work for projects the daemon has been contacted about*, AND NEVER *your projects are backed up*.** Whether a login-started daemon should back up projects it has never been contacted about is new per-user state at the cut and is hv's (routed 2026-08-30, vc recommending NARROW-not-BUILD): **if it is ruled in, this row WIDENS VISIBLY rather than turning out to have covered it all along.**

**THE REPORTING HALF HAS A FALSIFIER AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE.** `hours_since_last_good_snapshot` filters `outcome = 'ok'`, so it reads only SUCCESSES: a store failing every scheduled backup for a week reports *the newest restorable snapshot is 168h old* and never *because seven attempts failed, most recently: disk full*. **The detail exists in the store and surfaces only in `backup --list`, which is the log nobody reads in this row's own first paragraph.** That is `IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001`. **SO: `doctor` distinguishing NEVER TRIED from TRIED AND FAILED is a closing condition of this row, and its absence falsifies the row.**

**AND THE EMPTY POPULATION IS WITNESSED RATHER THAN GUARDED, BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE MADE UNREPRESENTABLE -- empty-at-boot is CORRECT.** `daemon status` grows a per-project listing so an operator can see the registry is empty; the per-project state is **DERIVED at read time** from `hours_since_last_good_snapshot`, not stored, so no `scheduled` field exists to go stale (hv's menubar ruling on `AC-01.8`, same shape). **cc considered `scheduled: bool` on `RegisteredProject` and refused it for want of a reader -- correct, and the resolution is that the listing makes the field UNNECESSARY rather than justified.**

**WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: two implementations of the backup cycle; a skipped, deferred or failed backup visible only in `backup --list`; `doctor` unable to distinguish never-tried from tried-and-failed; or a registry an operator cannot observe.**
